results.collection_method_note: Three collection forks ran in parallel, each scoped to a disjoint slice of resources/sources.md, mirroring the 2026-10-26/2026-11-02 approach: (1) cloud-native tech + Seattle-area majors, (2) energy-sector + Palantir/Leidos, (3) newly-formalized/promising-leads/aggregators + a fresh discovery sweep for brand-new sources. Each fork performed its own Step 3.5 live-URL validation inline (WebFetch first, ATS JSON API fallback for Workday/Lever/Ashby/some Greenhouse SPA renders) and did not write any files or commit. The orchestrating main thread compiled all 3 forks' qualifying roles (24 total, 1 cross-fork duplicate), curated to 15 for quality/redundancy (see dropped list below), wrote the report/log, updated resources/sources.md, attempted the dashboard update, and committed.

token_usage.note: Exact figures for all 3 collection forks, taken directly from their completion notifications. Main-thread usage is not measurable precisely; proxy below.

main_thread_tool_calls_estimate.note: Main thread (orchestrator) made zero independent collection calls this run — all primary collection/filtering/Step-3.5 validation was performed by the 3 forks above. Main thread read sources.md/workflow/prior logs, compiled/curated 24 qualifying roles down to 15, wrote the report/log, edited resources/sources.md, and handled the dashboard update and commit.

timing.note: step2 wall-clock time approximated from the longest-running fork's duration_ms (~784s); the 3 forks ran concurrently rather than sequentially, so this is far less than the sum of their individual durations (~25 min serial equivalent).
